newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-German, Austria shares climb to record highs.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-German, Austria shares climb to record highs.

text.p: German and Austrian shares closed on Tuesday at record highs, boosted by the strong dollar, but British stocks tumbled on inflation worries.
The dollar rose above 1.76 marks for the first time since February 1994 in late Europe but fell to its session low versus the yen.
The yen strengthened before Japanese trade data due at 2350 GMT. Most analysts expected Japan's trade surplus with the U.S. to widen and bolster the yen.
In metals, gold bounced off 12-year lows. New York gold futures opened higher on light fund buying after six consecutive days of declines.
But traders said spot gold remained vulnerable to $314 per ounce and possibly, falling below $300 within a few months.
Precious metals "have been going sideways for so long that now a trend has started. It will be very significant," said Fran Skelley, analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston.

The dollar's recent strength versus the mark lifted German export shares, which led the DAX index to a sixth consecutive record high close. The DAX ended bourse trade up 33.56 points, or 0.8 percent, at 4,006.40.
Siemens AG hit a year high in Frankfurt after Britain's General Electric Co Plc said it was reviewing its GPT telecoms venture with Siemens.
Siemens ended up 0.10 mark at 108.75, off its year high of 110.10 set early in the day.
Retailer Metro AG extended Monday's rally after Metro said it was talking with Dutch retailer SHV Holdings NV about taking over its cash and carry business.
Metro shares finished up 10.90 marks at 216.40, off its year high of 219.00 set earlier in the day.
Austrian shares also climbed to their seventh consecutive record high close on the ATX index.
Oil and chemicals group OMV AG led the advance, surging 53 schillings to a year high of 1,677 before profit-taking emerged. OMV closed at 1,673, up 3.27 percent.

"The (ATX index's) basic tendency is positive, but the steep advance is over for the time being," a trader said. Most traders expected the ATX index to consolidate between 1,370 and 1,400 points in the near-term.
But those gains, the dollar's support for most European export shares and the Dow Jones Industrial Average's higher opening in New York failed to pull other European bourses higher.

France's CAC-40 index slid, with Alcatel Alsthom among the biggest losers. Alcatel shed 2.02 percent to 775 French francs after Britain's General Electric Co Plc said it was talking with Alcatel about the future of their GEC Alsthom joint venture.
Alcatel had no comment on the news.
London's FTSE-100 index fell on interest rate and currency nerves after signs of rising inflation.
British government debt prices fell, pushing long-term interest rates up, after Britain's June retail price index (RPI) rose 0.4 percent to exceed forecasts for a 0.2-percent increase.
The RPI jump reinforced expectations the Bank of England would raise official rates by at least 25 basis points at the end of its two-day policy meeting on Thursday.

"The market is anxious about rates," a dealer said. "If (Bank of England) doesn't move, the market will go down. If rates are raised by a quarter (point), it will not be enough. And if they go by half a point, it (will) be perceived as a lack of confidence in (finance minister Gordon) Brown."

If rates rise, traders worried sterling would climb further and chip away more profits from British companies with substantial overseas exposure as a strong currency makes their goods and services more expensive abroad.
Sterling hit a six-year high versus the mark after the retail price report.
A leading business survey said British engineering firms' second-quarter export orders fell to the lowest in three years because of the pound's surge.
Against the dollar, the pound slid back below 1.69.

In New York, the Dow was up 46.82 points at 7,905.31 at 1545 GMT. The Dow was boosted by bargain-hunting after Monday's downturn and active technology stocks before earning results due after New York's close.
CURRENCIES AT THE CLOSE
The dollar was at 112.73 yen and 1.7587 marks compared with 112.30 and 1.7458 in late Europe on Monday.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index ended down 52.2 points, or 1.09 percent, at 4,758.50.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed bourse trading up 33.56 points at 4,006.40.
PARIS - The CAC-40 ended down 17.85 points at 2,929.81.
PRECIOUS METALS

Gold ended firmer in London at $321.95 per ounce, from $318.55 at Monday's close. Silver ended down nine cents at $4.36, up from a near four-year low fixing earlier at $4.25 and from $4.45 at Monday's close.
